sink: glob(`${logDir}/mcp*.log`) / glob(`${logDir}/*.log`) / readdir(logDir) then readFile() on each match, contents returned to caller
why: The tool's description says 'Read MCP logs from the standard location', but customPath completely overrides that default with zero validation, no containment check, and no restriction to any actual log directory. A caller can set customPath to any directory (e.g. a user's home directory or /var/log) and the handler will glob for '*.log' files there (falling back from 'mcp*.log' to any '*.log' file) and return up to 500KB of their contents. This discloses the content of arbitrary '*.log'-named files anywhere the server process can read, not just genuine MCP logs.
contract: Read MCP logs from the standard location

guard: bypassable: startsWith() prefix check with no trailing-separator boundary
why: validatePath() resolves and normalizes the requested path, then checks containment with normalized.startsWith(dir) where dir is one of the allowed directories -- but startsWith() performs a plain string-prefix match with no check that the next character is a path separator. If the server is restricted to e.g. '/home/user/safe', a path such as '/home/user/safe_bak/exfil.txt' or '/home/user/safe-evil/x' also satisfies the startsWith('/home/user/safe') check even though it is a sibling directory entirely outside the intended jail, letting a caller read from or write to any directory that merely shares the allowed directory's name as a string prefix. In the common no-CLI-args deployment (allowedDirectories defaults to [process.cwd()]), this is directly exploitable against any sibling of the working directory.
contract: All specified paths must be within allowed directories if specified.

why: params.collection is split with dirname()/basename() but neither function removes shell metacharacters -- both halves are still raw caller-controlled substrings. They (plus environment and each variables entry) are pushed into an argv array that is then joined with spaces into ONE string and passed to exec(), which spawns via /bin/sh -c. A collection path such as '/tmp/x; touch /tmp/pwned; echo y/z.bru' becomes dirname='/tmp/x; touch /tmp/pwned; echo y', basename='z.bru', producing the shell command 'cd /tmp/x; touch /tmp/pwned; echo y && bru run z.bru ...' -- the injected 'touch' command executes. environment and variables entries are equally unescaped and reach the same joined string.

sink: execAsync(<command string>) -- runs through a shell
guard: bypassable: code.replace(/"/g,'\\"') blindly escapes every quote regardless of a preceding backslash
why: Running caller-supplied Babashka code is this tool's stated purpose, so that alone is not the finding -- the finding is that the quoting meant to confine `code` inside the -e "..." shell argument is bypassable, letting a caller break out into arbitrary OS shell commands (not just babashka code). Concretely: code ending in a literal backslash immediately before an embedded quote (raw chars ...\\") becomes ...\\\\" after the replace (the pre-existing backslash plus the replacement's escaped quote = two backslashes then a bare quote). Bash reads \\\\ inside the double-quoted string as one escaped literal backslash, leaving the following " unescaped, which closes the quoted argument early. Everything after that point in `code` is then parsed as literal, unquoted shell input -- e.g. a code value shaped as foo\\"; touch /tmp/pwned # produces the shell sequence `bb -e "foo\\"; touch /tmp/pwned #"`, which runs the injected `touch` command and comments out the dangling trailing quote. Same escaping-bypass class as spencerhhubert/illustrator-mcp-server's AppleScript sink elsewhere in this corpus.

sink: node:fs/promises readFile(input) -- reads the given path as a local file when it isn't an http(s)/data: URL
guard: partial: only a recognized image file extension (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.gif/.webp) is accepted; no directory restriction
why: resolveImageInput() reads any local path whose extension matches a known image MIME type and base64-embeds its content into the outbound request to xAI's image-edit API -- there is no jail to any upload/staging directory, only an extension allowlist. A caller cannot read arbitrary text files (they'd be rejected as 'unsupported image format'), but any locally-readable file that happens to already have one of those five extensions -- regardless of its actual content -- gets read and transmitted to a third-party API, and the description explicitly advertises 'local file paths' as a supported input form for image_urls. Filed Tier B: the extension gate meaningfully narrows real-world impact compared to the twikit-style unrestricted case elsewhere in this corpus.
contract: Provide 1-3 source images (as URLs, base64 data URIs, or local file paths)
